metadata.title: Quantum gates and algorithms in qg units: Hamming-weight conservation, readout classes and the local radius

creators.name: Monteverde, Vicente Humberto
creators.affiliation: Universidad del Museo Social Argentino (UMSA), Argentina

metadata.description: We write fifteen standard quantum gates and fourteen standard quantum algorithms in qg units. An n-qubit state is described by its qg values, qg_P=⟨ P⟩ for every Pauli string P, and a gate U acts as qg_P'=qg_U^† PU. With this one rule each gate becomes a table of qg transformations and each algorithm a readout identity: which qg values hold the answer. The formulation is the Pauli (Heisenberg) representation and adds no new physics. It gives three practical classifications in the units used by the rest of the qang project: which gates conserve Hamming weight, and therefore admit the qg symmetry witness and filter; which algorithms are read out from a few qg values and which need the full outcome histogram; and where reading qg values is strictly worse than the standard readout. Three readout identities are, as far as we know, not stated in this form elsewhere: the per-qubit polar bias after Grover iterations, Simon's secret as the unique non-trivial Z-parity equal to one, and quantum counting as a single qg_X. We then restate every gate and algorithm with the local radius of each qubit, r_q^2=qg_X^2+qg_Y^2+qg_Z^2, the radius of the sphere on which the qubit lives (area 4π r_q^2). For a pure global state 1-r_q^2 is the known one-tangle; for a noisy state it mixes entanglement and noise. In a state of fixed Hamming weight r_q=|qg_Z|, so the radius is read from Z-basis shots alone, and under equal T_1 the qg filter restores it exactly: in a pre-registered simulation the filtered deficit equals the noiseless tangle to 3×10^-15, while the unfiltered readout reports a false deficit of 0.60–0.95 on product states. Every identity is checked numerically and pinned by tests in the open-source library qang (version 0.6.4, pip install qang), module qang.formulation.
metadata.notes: Every numerical claim is reproduced by the open-source library qang (pip install qang, version 0.6.17) and pinned by its tests; predictions were committed before each run.
